solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Drunk in classic style, as energy drinks might be

indicators.note: the drunk is placed in the middle of the classic style, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: Ionic is one of the classical orders of Greek architecture
a sot is a habitual drunkard

explanation.surface: A refined drinker sips an energy drink in classical fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports and energy drinks are often marketed as matching the body's own salt concentration, the technical sense of the term.

clue.text: Influence politician to support one piece of legislation

indicators.note: in a down clue the politician holds up the one from below, so it follows it

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MP stands for Member of Parliament
an act is a law passed by a parliament

explanation.surface: A lobbyist sways a politician into backing a single bill.
explanation.definitionFit: An effect or strong influence on something, as a noun or verb synonym.

clue.text: Businesspeople sign to get investment of banks in Israel

indicators.note: investment is putting inside, so the sign is invested with the chosen letters

parts.note: an omen is a sign of things to come

indicators.note: the banks of a word are its outer letters, the first and last of Israel

explanation.surface: Financiers take a portent as a cue to invest in Israeli banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks in' takes IL from IsraeL; 'investment' is placement, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Owners and executives of petroleum companies are people engaged in a particular industry.

clue.text: No kids left in deep pool abroad

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed among the rearranged letters
abroad means all over the place, so the letters of deep pool are scattered

explanation.surface: No children allowed into a deep swimming pool overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly folk are the opposite of kids, the young, so the definition works by contrast.

clue.text: Home's tip with vermin about, providing hardship

indicators.note: about means all around, so these letters are tossed about into a new order

parts.note: taken with the S, a home is

explanation.surface: A rubbish tip near the house is overrun with rats, causing misery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' is a British word for a rubbish dump.
explanation.definitionFit: Poverty and destitution bring want and suffering, so the noun is a synonym for hardship.

clue.text: Some meeting Italian around fire

indicators.note: the run taken from the two words is turned round, read from right to left
only some of the letters of the following words are used, a run sitting across the two

explanation.surface: A few people gather with an Italian around a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes ETINGI from meETING Italian, and 'around' turns it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire something, as a fuel or a fuse, is to set it alight: a straightforward verb synonym.

clue.text: Obstruct fool?

parts.note: a mug is a fool; written upward in a down light, the word for fool reads as the first part of the answer

explanation.surface: Is obstructing someone foolish?
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: GUM 'up' in a down entry reads MUG, a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: To clog machinery with sticky matter is to obstruct it.

clue.text: Clubs comprising first satirical writers

indicators.note: comprising means containing, so the clubs hold the abbreviation for first

parts.note: irons are golf clubs
1st, written IST, is the short form of first

explanation.surface: Golf clubs that include the leading satirists among members.
explanation.definitionFit: Writers who use irony, saying the opposite of what is meant, are close kin to satirists.

clue.text: Meeting that is around first of December when it's becoming darker

parts.note: an event is a meeting or occasion

indicators.note: the abbreviation for that is goes around the opening letter of December

parts.note: i.e. abbreviates id est, Latin for that is

indicators.note: first of means the opening letter of December

explanation.surface: A gathering in early December as the nights draw in.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, the time of day when the light fades.

clue.text: Recycling, pretty busy with axe and a long old length of carpet

indicators.note: recycling means reprocessing, so the letters of these words are reused in a new order

explanation.surface: A busy recycling scene: something pretty, an axe and an old roll of carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bayeux Tapestry is an embroidered cloth about 70 metres long showing the Norman Conquest of 1066, so 'carpet' is loose but playful.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient embroidered strip of linen nearly 70 metres long, playfully called a length of floor covering.

clue.text: Rejected dessert with European sauce accumulated

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the whole string of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: pud is short for pudding, a British word for dessert
lip, like sauce, means cheeky impudence

explanation.surface: A diner sends back a pudding with its sauce, which had built up on the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns PUD + E + LIP, giving PILEDUP. Sauce here is cheek, not gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that have piled up have built up in a heap, so the phrase is a synonym for gathered together.

clue.text: Supply equipment to fix part of jacket

parts.note: to arm someone is to supply them with weapons or equipment
a hole is a fix or predicament, as in being in a hole

explanation.surface: A tailor supplies the tools needed to mend a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening in a jacket or garment through which the arm passes is a structural part of it.

clue.text: Island's found, not Australia

indicators.note: 'not' says the letter for Australia is left out of the word for found

parts.note: to found something is to create or establish it
A is the international vehicle code for Australia

explanation.surface: An island has been discovered, and it is not Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' reads as the past of find, but it is the verb meaning establish.
explanation.definitionFit: The largest of the Greek islands, in the Mediterranean, home of the Minoan civilisation.

clue.text: Slant that might be found on hill

definitions.meaning: a slant is a particular angle or perspective on an issue

definitions.text: that might be found on hill
definitions.meaning: a spot on high ground from which a scenic outlook can be enjoyed

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an opinion or angle on a matter and a literal place from which to look out over scenery.

clue.text: Rough team after a savage prop before match day

indicators.note: the team's letters come after a and the reworked prop
savage means wild or brutal, so the letters of the word prop are roughed up into a new order

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a football or cricket team
to mate is to match or pair up

explanation.surface: A rugby match report: a savage prop forward, then the team, ahead of the match day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'savage' rearranges the forward's letters. 'prop' and 'match' sit in a rugby scene but are fodder and a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough figure or sketch is one only approximately right, an estimate rather than an exact value.

clue.text: Confusion beginning to mount after learner's introduced to eminent composer

indicators.note: the opening letter of mount comes after the rest
the learner's letter is introduced into the word for an eminent composer

parts.note: a maestro is a distinguished composer or conductor
L is the learner sign, the L-plate on British cars

indicators.note: beginning means the first letter of mount

explanation.surface: A great composer's chaos as a pupil joins him on the podium.
explanation.definitionFit: A whirlpool, used figuratively for a state of turmoil and chaos.

clue.text: Excessive pride from East European country with capital changed for good

indicators.note: the capital, the initial letter, of the country is swapped for the letter for good

parts.note: Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe

explanation.surface: An Eastern European nation's arrogance after it moved its capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like a capital city, but is the capital (first) letter, R.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive self-importance and vanity, an extreme form of pride.

clue.text: Princess gutted after horrific earful and outbursts

indicators.note: the gutted princess comes after the jumbled letters
horrific suggests something mangled, so the letters of earful are jumbled
gutted means the insides are removed, leaving only the outer letters of Princess

explanation.surface: A distraught princess after a horrible scolding and angry outbursts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrific' makes FLAREU from EARFUL; 'gutted' leaves PS of PrincesS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden flares of anger or violence are outbreaks, eruptions of temper or conflict.

clue.text: They did row and cry about being in Las Vegas broke

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, the reversed cry sitting in the rearranged city name
broke means broken, so the letters of the city are smashed and reassembled
about here means turned round, so the cry is written backwards

parts.note: to yell is to cry out loudly

explanation.surface: Someone argued and wept on finding themselves penniless in Las Vegas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broke' rearranges the city's letters, and the cry turned 'about' goes inside them. 'row' is rowing a boat, not a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Convicts and captives chained to oars powered ancient and early-modern warships by rowing.

clue.text: Stop sibling getting enthralled by one that's stuffed up

indicators.note: enthralled means captivated, held in, so the sibling is held within the other piece
in a down clue, up means the word is written from the bottom upward

parts.note: a ted, short for teddy bear, is a stuffed toy
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A sibling transfixed by someone stuffy is told to stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one that's stuffed' is a teddy bear, a stuffed toy; 'up' turns it over before the sibling goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To desist is to cease or refrain from an action: a formal synonym for halt.

clue.text: Cockney's hound biting overturned alien vessel

indicators.note: biting means holding in the teeth, so the hound encloses the reversed alien
a Cockney, a working-class Londoner, drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: to harry someone is to hound or harass them

indicators.note: overturned means flipped, so the alien's letters are reversed

parts.note: E.T. is the alien from the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A Cockney's dog bites a capsized alien spaceship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney's' drops the H, giving ARRY; 'overturned' makes TE. 'hound' is a verb, not a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A blood vessel carrying blood away from the heart, the sense of vessel used in anatomy.

clue.text: Others arrived to go round second-rate seaside town

parts.note: more means additional ones, others

indicators.note: the word for arrived wraps around the letter for second-rate

parts.note: came is the past tense of come, meaning arrived
B is a grade below A, hence second-rate

explanation.surface: More visitors turned up at a shabby seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: MORECAMBE is a seaside town on the Lancashire coast in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort on Morecambe Bay in Lancashire, a classic English holiday town by the sea.

clue.text: One who tends to rush half- heartedly

indicators.note: half-heartedly means half of the heart is removed: the two middle letters lose one

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong

explanation.surface: Someone inclined to hurry, but only half committed.
explanation.walkthrough: CAREER has EE at its heart; losing half leaves one E. 'tends' is caring for someone, not inclining.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who looks after a sick, elderly or disabled person, tending to their needs.

clue.text: Hot in brown fleece

indicators.note: the letter for hot goes inside the word for brown

parts.note: to sear meat is to brown it quickly over high heat
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A warm brown fleece jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' looks like a noun, a garment, but is the verb meaning clip wool from a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: To fleece a sheep is to remove its wool by clipping, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Gas about duster regularly getting particle

indicators.note: the gas wraps about the letters chosen from duster

parts.note: neon is a noble gas

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of duster is taken, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: Gas swirls round a duster, regularly picking up particles.
explanation.definitionFit: A subatomic particle with no electric charge, found in the nucleus of an atom alongside protons.

clue.text: Dog virtually seizes new dish

indicators.note: the shortened dog takes hold of the letter for new, holding it inside
virtually means almost, so the dog's breed name loses its final letter

parts.note: a terrier is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: A dog all but grabs a newly served dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'virtually' cuts the last letter, giving TERRIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthenware cooking dish, and the pâté cooked and served in it.

clue.text: Give confidence when very well

parts.note: as can mean when, as in as I left
sure is an informal reply meaning very well or certainly

explanation.surface: A boost to someone's confidence when they are in fine health.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassure or convince someone is to give them confidence; the verb and phrase are synonyms.

clue.text: Extremely sexy Madame to aim for shapely attribute

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme letters, the first and last of sexy

parts.note: to try is to aim or attempt

explanation.surface: A seductive madame aims for a curvaceous figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Balance of proportions, each side matching the other, is a mark of good form or beauty.
